Name: Forms
Summary: Contact forms, quote requests and other forms that editors build in the admin, with an inbox for the answers and an optional e-mail for each one.
Guide:
Each instance holds one form. Add an instance per form: a site can have contact and quote side by side, each with its own fields, inbox and template.

Add it to the site

app.Use(
    forms.Module("contact", "Contact"),
    forms.Module("quote", "Quote request"),
)

The key (contact) is the instance's name in URLs and templates and must be unique on the site. The title (Contact) is what editors see in the admin navigation and the page editor.

Build the form

In the admin, open the instance (/admin/contact; /admin is the default admin path) and choose New form. An instance has one form, so the button disappears once it exists. The form has a title, an introduction and a success message (both Markdown), its fields, and an optional Notification e-mail.

Fields are written as text, one per line: name | type | label | placeholder | help. A * after the name makes the field required; placeholder and help are optional. The options of a select follow on their own lines, starting with -:

name* | text | Name
email* | email | E-mail | you@example.com
topic | select | Topic
- sales | Sales
- support | Support
message* | textarea | Message | | Tell us what you need.
terms* | checkbox | I agree to the privacy statement
  • Types: text, email, textarea, select, checkbox, number and date.
  • Names use lowercase letters, digits and underscores, start with a letter, and are unique. website is taken by the spam trap.
  • A form has at most 50 fields, a select at most 100 options.
  • Names, types and options are shared by all languages; labels, placeholders, help and option labels belong to the language being edited. A field without a label in the visitor's language shows its name.

Publish the form when it is ready. It is shown in each language that has a title, a success message and field labels.

While the form is on a page, links to addresses on the site in its introduction and success message count for Links to a page: the editor of a page lists the form when it links there, and Pages › Broken links lists its links that lead nowhere.

Place it on a page

In the admin, open a page and choose the instance under Shows on this page. The page shows the form at its own address and receives it there too, with contact/form.gohtml, or forms/form.gohtml for every form without a design of its own. Generate a complete working starting point, with every kind of field:

task templates -- contact

A minimal template:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/forms.FormView */}}
<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>

{{if .Sent}}
    {{.Success}}
{{else}}
    {{.Intro}}

    {{if .Throttled}}<p>You sent this form several times already. Please try again later.</p>{{end}}
    {{if .Invalid}}<p>Please check the marked fields.</p>{{end}}

    {{form_render .Form .Errors}}
{{end}}

.Form is the form as the editor built it, in the page's language. form_render renders all of it with go-form: each field with its label, placeholder, help text and limits, the visitor's answers and the errors of a post at their fields, the spam trap and a Send button, translated with the site's translations and in the site's form theme. The fields' ids start with the instance key, such as contact-email.

To lay out the fields yourself, write the form with form_open, form_field per name in .Fields and form_close:

{{form_open .Form}}
    {{range .Fields}}
        {{form_field $.Form . $.Errors}}
    {{end}}
    <button type="submit">Send</button>
{{form_close}}

form_field renders a field by its name, email for example, so a template can also place the fields one by one. See Template functions.

Visitors

The form posts to the page itself (.Action), not to a visitor action under /_/, but it is protected the same way.

  • With errors, the page shows the form again with status 422, the visitor's answers, .Invalid set and .Errors: go-form's messages in the page's language, which form_render and form_field show at their fields.
  • After a valid submission the visitor returns to the page with ?sent=1, such as /en/contact?sent=1, and .Sent is set: show .Success instead of the form.
  • form_open and form_render add the spam trap. Bots that fill it in are told the form was sent; nothing is stored.
  • Posts from other sites are refused by cross-origin protection. The form needs no token or cookie, so it never expires, however long it stays open.
  • Each visitor may send the form 10 times in 10 minutes, posts with errors included. After that the form is shown again with .Throttled set and their answers kept, with status 429; nothing is stored.

Values are checked by type, with go-form's validation: a text is one line of at most 500 characters, a textarea at most 10,000, an email one address mail can be sent to, as the site's other forms check it (mail.Rule, see Addresses in forms), so anna@localhost is refused, a number a number, a date a YYYY-MM-DD date and a select one of its options. A checkbox is stored as yes or no.

Inbox

Submissions on the form's admin page opens the inbox (/admin/contact/inbox), with tabs for new, archived and all submissions, dated in the site's timezone. The badge in the navigation counts the new ones.

A submission keeps the answers with the labels the visitor saw and the language they used, so later changes to the form leave it unchanged. Editors archive a handled submission or move it back to new; Move to trash moves it to the trash, where it can be restored or deleted for good. Archiving needs the edit right, deleting the delete right. Trash on the inbox lists the deleted submissions.

E-mail

When the form has a notification address, every submission is mailed there in the admin's language. By default the subject is the form's title in the visitor's language; the text lists each answer under its label, followed by a link to the submission in the admin. Replying goes to the first address the visitor gave in an email field.

The mail is the template notify, with a forms.NotifyView. A theme replaces it with mail/contact/notify.gohtml, or mail/forms/notify.gohtml for every form; task templates -- contact writes the default there. The submission is stored first; a mail that fails is only logged.

From Go

forms.Of(app, "contact") returns the instance once the app has started. It reads and handles submissions the way the inbox does:

contact := forms.Of(app, "contact")

waiting, err := contact.Count(ctx, forms.StatusNew)
latest, more, err := contact.SubmissionsByStatus(ctx, forms.StatusNew, 0, 20)

An empty status lists or counts every submission. Submission reads one, and Archive, Unarchive, DeleteSubmission, UndeleteSubmission and PurgeSubmission take a submission ID; the last three move a submission to the trash, bring it back or remove it for good. For seed data, ParseFields reads fields in the editor's syntax and Store() saves the form:

fields, labels, err := forms.ParseFields("name* | text | Name\nemail* | email | E-mail\nmessage* | textarea | Message\n")

form, err := contact.Store().Save(ctx, content.Draft[forms.Definition, forms.Text]{
    Fields: forms.Definition{Fields: fields, Notify: "info@example.com"},
    Translations: content.SetText(nil, "en", forms.Text{
        Title:   "Contact",
        Success: "Thank you. We reply within two working days.",
        Labels:  labels,
    }),
})

err = contact.Store().Publish(ctx, form.ID, "", "en")

Related modules

  • Registrations handles sign-ups for events, with places, prices and a confirmation mail.
  • Submissions lets visitors send in news that editors accept as a draft post.
  • Newsletter collects e-mail addresses with double opt-in.

Templates.Name: form

Fields.Name: Action
Fields.Doc: Action is the URL the form posts to: the page itself.

Fields.Name: Form
Fields.Doc: Form is the form's model: its fields as the editor defined them, in the page's language, with the visitor's answers after a post with errors, for go-form's template functions, such as {{form_render .Form .Errors}}, or {{form_open .Form}} with {{form_field .Form name .Errors}} per name of Fields. form_open adds the spam trap (frontend.Honeypot), and the fields' ids start with the instance key.

Fields.Name: Fields
Fields.Doc: Fields are the names of the form's fields, in order, for form_field.

Fields.Name: Errors
Fields.Doc: Errors are the problems of a post per field, with messages in the page's language, which form_field and form_render show at their fields; empty otherwise.

Fields.Name: Invalid
Fields.Doc: Invalid is set when a submission has errors; see Errors.

Fields.Name: Throttled
Fields.Doc: Throttled is set when the visitor sent the form too often in a short time. Nothing was stored; the form is shown with their answers, to send again later.

Fields.Name: Sent
Fields.Doc: Sent is set after a successful submission; show Success instead of the form.

Mail.Name: notify

Fields.Name: Title
Fields.Doc: Title is the form's title in the language the visitor used.

Fields.Name: Locale
Fields.Doc: Locale is the language the visitor used.

Fields.Name: Answers
Fields.Doc: Answers are the submitted values, each with the label the visitor saw.

Fields.Name: ReplyTo

Fields.Doc: SubmissionURL opens the submission in the admin.

SQL.Name: postgres
SQL.SQL:
-- Form definitions are a collection (see package content); an instance holds
-- one form. Fields and labels are JSON; notify is the address that receives
-- new submissions.
CREATE TABLE wt_forms_form (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    instance    VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    published   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    position    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by  UUID,
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by  UUID,
    deleted_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    deleted_by  UUID,
    form_fields TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    notify      VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

CREATE INDEX wt_forms_form_instance ON wt_forms_form (instance);

CREATE TABLE wt_forms_form_translation (
    item_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES wt_forms_form (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    locale       VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    title        VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    intro        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    success      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    field_labels TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, locale)
);

-- Submissions belong to the instance, so they outlive changes to the form.
-- Answers are JSON with the labels the visitor saw. Status is new or archived.
CREATE TABLE wt_forms_submission (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    locale     VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    status     VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new',
    answers    TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by UUID,
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID,
    deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    deleted_by UUID
);

CREATE INDEX wt_forms_submission_instance ON wt_forms_submission (instance, created_at);

CREATE INDEX wt_forms_submission_status ON wt_forms_submission (instance, status, created_at);

SQL.Name: mysql
SQL.SQL:
-- Form definitions are a collection (see package content); an instance holds
-- one form. Fields and labels are JSON; notify is the address that receives
-- new submissions.
CREATE TABLE wt_forms_form (
    id          VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    instance    VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    published   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    position    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at  DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    created_by  VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    updated_at  DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_by  VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    deleted_at  DATETIME(6) NULL,
    deleted_by  VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    form_fields TEXT NOT NULL,
    notify      VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    INDEX wt_forms_form_instance (instance)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE wt_forms_form_translation (
    item_id      VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
    locale       VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    title        VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    intro        TEXT NOT NULL,
    success      TEXT NOT NULL,
    field_labels TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, locale),
    FOREIGN KEY (item_id) REFERENCES wt_forms_form (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

-- Submissions belong to the instance, so they outlive changes to the form.
-- Answers are JSON with the labels the visitor saw. Status is new or archived.
CREATE TABLE wt_forms_submission (
    id         VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    locale     VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    status     VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new',
    answers    MEDIUMTEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    created_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    updated_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    deleted_at DATETIME(6) NULL,
    deleted_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    INDEX wt_forms_submission_instance (instance, created_at),
    INDEX wt_forms_submission_status (instance, status, created_at)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

Types.Name: Answer
Types.Doc: Answer is one submitted value, with the label the visitor saw.

Types.Name: Answers
Types.Doc: Answers is stored as JSON in one column.

Types.Name: Definition
Types.Doc: Definition is the language-independent part of a form. Notify is the address new submissions are mailed to; empty sends no mail.

Types.Name: Field
Types.Doc: Field is one input of the form. Labels are translated; see Label.

Types.Name: FieldList
Types.Doc: FieldList is stored as JSON in one column.

Types.Name: FormView
InboxRow
Types.Doc: InboxRow is one submission in the inbox; Summary shows its first answers.
Types.Decl:
type InboxRow struct {
	URL      string
	Date     string
	Locale   string
	Summary  string
	Archived bool
}

Types.Name: InboxView
Types.Doc: InboxView is the data of templates/admin/inbox.gohtml: the submissions of a form, filtered by status.

Types.Name: Item
Types.Doc: Item is a stored form with its translations.

Types.Name: Label
Types.Doc: Label is the text of one field in one language. Options maps option values to their labels.

Types.Name: Labels
Types.Doc: Labels maps field names to their text; stored as JSON in one column.

Types.Name: NotifyView
Types.Doc: NotifyView is the data of the mail template notify, sent to the form's notification address in the admin's language. Replying answers the visitor when the form has an email field.

Types.Name: Service
Types.Doc: Service is one form, for the website's own code.

Types.Name: Submission
Types.Doc: Submission is one sent form. DeletedAt and DeletedBy are set for submissions in the trash (see TrashedSubmissions).
Types.Decl:
type Submission struct {
	ID        string     `db:"id"`
	Locale    string     `db:"locale"`
	Status    string     `db:"status"`
	Answers   Answers    `db:"answers"`
	CreatedAt time.Time  `db:"created_at"`
	DeletedAt *time.Time `db:"deleted_at"`
	DeletedBy db.Ref     `db:"deleted_by"`
}

Types.Name: SubmissionView
Types.Doc: SubmissionView is the data of templates/admin/submission.gohtml: one submission with every answer.
Types.Decl:
type SubmissionView struct {
	Title    string
	BackURL  string
	Date     string
	Locale   string
	Archived bool
	Answers  Answers
	// Archive or Unarchive is set, depending on the status, for editors.
	Archive   *form.RenderModel
	Unarchive *form.RenderModel
	Delete    *form.RenderModel
}

Types.Name: Text
Types.Doc: Text is a form in one language. Intro and Success are Markdown.
